newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Peters surprised New Zealand dlr reacts to comment.
newsitem.headline: Peters surprised New Zealand dlr reacts to comment.

text.p: New Zealand Deputy Prime Minister and Treasurer Winston Peters said on Monday he was surprised the New Zealand dollar had reacted to his forecast that the currency would appreciate further.
Peters told reporters after a brief meeting with Singapore leaders he had been commenting on a long-term trend.
"We've had a dollar that rose from 44 cents in March 1985 to where it is today," he said.

"We intend to run a low inflation regime, to manage the government's costs down, and in that climate I am somewhat astonished that the marketplace would think that comments about the dollar rising in the long, long-term is in any way a remarkable statement."
The Kiwi firmed slightly in early trade on Monday after Peters told Reuters Financial Television in an interview on Sunday "in the long term the (New Zealand) dollar will go on rising".
The currency fell back again later in the day. It closed at US$0.6893/00.
